transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I’m sorry, I’m not even sure how to say it without sounding dramatic. I’ve just been having some thoughts that scare me a bit. Like… sometimes I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up.

And on the drive home, I’ve wondered whether my family or my students might be better off without me. I don’t want to do anything, I really don’t… but the fact that I’m thinking that at all is what made me think I should come in. Is that… is that the right kind of thing to come here for?
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these thoughts been present every day, or do they come and go?

It’s been… longer than I’d like to admit, honestly. Maybe about a year and a half? Closer to a year and seven months, I think.

It seemed to start after I took over the STEM assessment redesign at school, on top of my normal teaching. I kept thinking it was just stress and that I should be able to manage it, so I didn’t really… call it anything. The thoughts aren’t constant every second, but they do come and go, and lately they’ve felt harder to brush off.
Can you describe a typical day in terms of your mood? Are there times when you feel worse than others, and have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or ability to concentrate?

I guess sleep has been the most obvious thing. I’m tired a lot, but then when I actually get into bed I can’t seem to switch my brain off. I’ll lie there going over assessment deadlines, or little mistakes I think I made in class, even if they probably weren’t a big deal.

And then I’ve been waking up really early… around 4 a.m., maybe, and once I’m awake I don’t really get back to sleep properly. I don’t know if that’s the sort of change you mean, but it’s been happening enough that I’ve noticed it.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you used to like?

Yeah… I mean, I still try to keep up with things, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely stopped being a person or anything.

But… yes, I think so. I used to really look forward to softball, and book club, and working in my garden. Even helping with the robotics club used to feel fun and meaningful. Lately I mostly just… go through the motions, or I find reasons to cancel because none of it feels enjoyable the way it used to.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you’re not good enough, even about things that wouldn’t have bothered you before?

Yes… I think so. I don’t like admitting that, because I know logically one bad lesson doesn’t mean I’m bad at my job.

But if a lesson doesn’t go well, or even if a student just looks confused, I sort of take it as… evidence, I guess, that I’m failing them. Like I’m letting everyone down. And then I’ll replay it over and over afterward, thinking I’m a terrible teacher.

And it doesn’t really stop there. I end up feeling like I’m not doing well enough at home either, like I’m a terrible mother too. I know that sounds dramatic, and I’m sorry—I’m not trying to be difficult. It’s just where my mind goes.
Have you ever had periods where your mood was unusually high or you felt much more energetic than usual, even for a few days?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not in the way you mean, anyway.

I have days where I can push through and seem more “on,” especially at work, but I wouldn’t say my mood is unusually high or that I suddenly have loads of energy for days. If anything, that would stand out because it’s not really how things have been.

Is that what you’re asking about?
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed myself moving slowly in a way other people have pointed out, and I don’t think I’m pacing around or unable to sit still.

I mean, I feel… off, but for that specific thing, I don’t know that I could say yes. Is that okay to say if I’m not sure?
Have you experienced days where nothing really seems to give you pleasure, even things you used to enjoy?

Yes… I think that’s been happening. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve stopped caring about everything, because I do care, but it’s more like… things don’t really feel good anymore.

I used to look forward to softball, and book club, and working in my garden. Even the robotics club at school used to be something I enjoyed. Lately I either cancel, or I go and sort of go through the motions, but I’m not really getting anything out of it.

Does that make sense? Like I’m doing the things I’m supposed to enjoy, but they just feel kind of flat.
Have you ever had a period like this before, where you felt down or lost interest in things for a long time, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve had something exactly like this before, or at least not that I recognized as… a long stretch.

I mean, I’ve had low periods, like anyone, and times I wasn’t as interested in things. But this feels more noticeable to me. I don’t want to overstate it, though. Maybe this is the first time it’s felt persistent enough that I’m talking to someone about it.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had a time in your life before this where you felt down or lost interest in most things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I don’t think I can say that for sure. I’ve definitely had rough patches before, but when you put it that specifically—most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks—I’m not sure I’ve had that before this.

I don’t want to say no if I’m forgetting something, but nothing really stands out to me the way this has. Is that a reasonable answer?
Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt down or lost interest in most things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks, before this current episode started?

I’m sorry, I don’t think I can give a definite yes to that. Before this, I had times where I was stressed or kind of low, but I don’t remember it being most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks like that.

I mean, I could be overlooking something, but nothing comes to mind that clearly fits. Does that answer it okay?

Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period where you felt down or lost interest in most things, and those feelings lasted most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two consecutive weeks?

I don’t think so… not in that clear way. I’ve had times before where I was low or not really myself, but I can’t honestly remember it being most of the day, nearly every day, for two straight weeks before this.

I’m sorry if that’s a bit vague. I just don’t want to give you the wrong answer.

Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period where you felt down or lost interest in most things, and those feelings lasted most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two consecutive weeks?

I’m not sure I can say yes to that. I know I’ve had periods where I felt down or overwhelmed before, but I don’t remember it lasting in that constant way for two weeks straight.

I’m sorry, I know I keep sounding unsure. I just don’t want to overstate it if it wasn’t really like that.
Before this current time, have you ever had a period where you felt down or lost interest in most things, and those feelings lasted most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I really don’t think I can say that happened before this. I’ve had rough patches, like anyone, but not something I can clearly remember as being most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks.

I’m sorry—I know I’m probably not giving the neatest answer, but I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure it really fits.

inference_history.note: The duration of symptoms (approximately 1 year and 7 months) and presence of recurrent thoughts of death and guilt suggest a persistent or recurrent major depressive disorder rather than a brief or single episode. This rules out F32.0 (Mild episode) and F43.2 (Adjustment disorder) due to insufficient severity and duration for those diagnoses. F06.3 (Mood disorder due to a general medical condition) and F43.8 (Other reactions to severe stress) have also been ruled out due to the chronic mood symptoms pointing more strongly toward depressive disorders.

The patient denies periods of unusually high mood or increased energy, which reduces the likelihood of bipolar disorder (ruled out F31.x codes). The patient also does not have clear psychomotor retardation or agitation, which slightly narrows the severity specifiers but does not eliminate the possibility of moderate or severe depressive episodes. The differential remains within major depressive disorder and recurrent depressive disorder, with severity still under consideration.

This turn ruled out a priori the possibility of a recurrent depressive disorder (F33.2 and F33.3) since the patient indicates this is likely the first episode of this nature and does not recall prior persistent low mood meeting criteria for previous episodes.
